identity.title: Cirrhosis stigmata: spider angiomata, palmar erythema, gynecomastia, caput medusae, jaundice

technique.how: In good light inspect face, neck, upper chest, arms and back for spider angiomata (central arteriole with radiating vessels that blanch on central pressure and refill from the centre); inspect palms for thenar/hypothenar erythema, chest for gynecomastia, abdomen for dilated periumbilical veins, and sclerae/skin for jaundice.
technique.prerequisites: Adequate lighting; expose upper trunk and arms; glass slide or pen tip to blanch a spider.

interpretation.positive_finding: Spider nevi roughly quadruple the odds of biopsy-proven cirrhosis in patients with known or suspected liver disease (LR 4.3). Multiple stigmata together, especially with ascites or a low platelet count, make cirrhosis likely.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence of any single stigma does not exclude cirrhosis; compensated cirrhosis is often stigma-free, so rely on platelets, Lok index or imaging to rule out.
interpretation.pitfalls: Isolated spiders occur in pregnancy, estrogen use and healthy people; palmar erythema and gynecomastia have many non-hepatic causes; jaundice reflects hepatic dysfunction of any cause, not cirrhosis specifically.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: treat as probable cirrhosis and screen for ascites, encephalopathy and varices; negative: do not exclude cirrhosis without labs/imaging.

estimates.population: Adults with known or suspected liver disease; pooled 86 studies, 19,533 patients, 4,725 with biopsy-proven cirrhosis

sources.citation: Udell JA, Wang CS, Tinmouth J, et al. Does this patient with liver disease have cirrhosis? JAMA. 2012;307(8):832-842.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use stigmata to exclude cirrhosis before invasive procedures or drug dosing decisions; absence is uninformative.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Stigmata plus confusion, GI bleeding, fever with abdominal pain, or rising creatinine should prompt evaluation for hepatic encephalopathy, variceal bleeding, SBP or hepatorenal syndrome.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Interobserver agreement for individual stigmata is reported in the RCE tables (not viewable here); spider count and palmar erythema grading vary between examiners.

extraction_notes: Spider nevi LR+ 4.3 (95% CI 2.4-6.2) taken verbatim from the abstract of the 2012 RCE meta-analysis (PMID 22357834). The RCE tables also give LRs for palmar erythema, gynecomastia, jaundice, caput medusae and the negative LR of absent spiders, but the JAMA full text/tables are not accessible from this environment, so those estimates are left null. Only the positive direction is quantified here, hence partially_quantified. Prevalence 0.24 is the pooled prevalence across included studies.
